title: Oak Hollow Payments integration — call notes & action items
content:
Call date: 2026-09-25
Attendees: Elijah Smith (Oak Hollow - Eng), Priya Zhao (Oak Hollow - PM), Morgan Patel (Redwood SE), Riley Brooks (Redwood Solutions eng), Samira Khan (Redwood Sales eng)

Purpose: initial scoping call to capture Oak Hollow Payments' integration requirements and identify blockers for Dedicated vs Private deployment. They are evaluating Redwood for fraud-detection scoring and transaction categorization pipelines.

Summary notes:
- Oak Hollow wants low-latency scoring (<30ms p50, <100ms p95) for synchronous fraud checks integrated into their transaction pipeline (Kinesis -> validator -> Redwood call -> decision). Throughput estimate: 2000 TPS peak, steady-state 600 TPS.
- Primary concern: data residency & PCI scope. They prefer Redwood Private (VPC/on-prem) but are open to Dedicated if network restrictions can be satisfied (private peering + strict audit logs).
- Model: they plan to host a fine-tuned fraud model (Llama-3 variant) with a small contextual window. Need support for KV-cache across requests and pinned model versioning for rollouts.
- SLOs & SLA: expecting 99.95% uptime, support for incident bridge within 30 min for priority incidents. Also require audit logs for every inference request (request metadata, model version, latency, token usage).
- Security: KMS integration (AWS KMS + optional HSM), SSO/SCIM provisioning for team, per-customer key rotation policies.
- Networking: VPC peering + private IP access; fallback via dedicated-hosted endpoints if VPC unavailable.
- Observability: need token-level cost breakdown, per-route latency heatmap, and sampling of inputs/outputs for model drift monitoring (redacted PII).

Technical clarifications / gotchas called out:
- Oak Hollow's infra uses very short request payloads but high QPS; batching isn't helpful for latency SLOs — we should propose low-latency batching or continuous batching knobs.
- Model quantization: they want to reduce GPU footprint but are concerned about subtle accuracy regressions for fraud thresholds. Must provide evaluation harness (ROC/AUC comparison, false positive/negative analysis) as part of the onboarding.
- KV cache warmup: since transactions are often single-shot, caching might only help for session-based or recent-card histories. Need to confirm if they will include customer transaction history in the context.
- Data retention: legal requires inference logs to be retained for 7 years for audit; need to confirm Redwood's observability retention options and costs.
- Throughput planning: 2000 TPS peak => estimate of GPU nodes: initial approach = Dedicated pool with autoscale + burst to hosted if capacity exhausted. Need to provide cost estimate (monthly committed vs burst).

Action items / next steps:
1) Morgan to draft technical requirements doc and proposed architecture (Dedicated vs Private options) with network diagram and flow (due: 2026-09-29). Assignee: Morgan Patel.
2) Riley to run a perf profile on Llama-3-small quantized vs fp16 for similar fraud model (measure p50/p95 latency & token cost). Provide comparison table + recommended quantization level (due: 2026-10-02). Assignee: Riley Brooks.
3) Samira to coordinate with Solutions Pricing to produce a rough TCO for (a) Dedicated reserved capacity (monthly commit) and (b) Private (VPC + support) — include log retention costs at 7 years (due: 2026-10-05). Assignee: Samira Khan.
4) Elijah to share a sample of redacted transaction payloads (schema + 50 sample events) so we can run evaluation harness and check context window needs. He'll also confirm if historical transactions will be included in prompt context (due: 2026-09-28). Assignee: Elijah Smith (Oak Hollow).
5) Morgan to prepare a short eval plan for accuracy regression testing comparing baseline model (their current fraud scorer) vs Redwood-served variant; include metrics (precision@K, recall, AUC, fraud loss impact). Share Confluence page and link to OAK-56 ticket (due: 2026-10-06).
6) Security call: set up follow-up with Redwood Security to review KMS/HSM integration and SCIM/SSO provisioning. Proposed participants: Priya Natarajan (Redwood Security), Oak Hollow SecOps. Schedule: week of 2026-10-04.

Notes to self / conversational scraps:
- Need to check whether our private deployment package includes long-term audit log retention (7+ years) or if that's an add-on (I think add-on). Verify pricing model for archival logs (S3 glacier?).
- Confirm whether autoscale burst to hosted requires customer approval due to data residency (they will not allow data to leave VPC without double-check). If no, we need to propose hybrid routing (only metadata to hosted) — will need legal review.
- Look for previous similar account: "Harbor Financial" notes (see drive) — they had similar VPC + audit log ask; reuse architecture diagram.
- Reminder: bring up per-request redaction hooks and structured output + signature to make logs non-replayable.

Risks / blockers:
- Legal / compliance might block any cross-region or hosted fallback if Oak Hollow's PCI requirements are strict. Need early legal signoff.
- Quantization regressions could require more GPU capacity than projected, increasing cost. Make sure to include a sensitivity analysis.

Meeting follow-up items for next sync (tentative 1 week):
- Present architecture options (Dedicated vs Private) with cost delta + timeline
- Share perf experiment results + recommended quantization profile
- Confirm sample data ingestion & evaluation results
- Security deep-dive (KMS, SCIM, audit log retention)

Quick timeline (rough):
- 2026-09-28: sample event share from Oak Hollow
- 2026-09-29: Redwood draft architecture + network diagram
- 2026-10-02: perf results (Riley)
- 2026-10-05: TCO (Samira)
- 2026-10-06: eval plan pushed to Confluence & linked to OAK-56

End notes: keep this doc lightweight — will move to Confluence once architecture is stable. For now mark status: draft.

-- Morgan
